draft.title: Characterisation
card: Characterisation is how a writer builds a character for the reader. A writer can use direct description, which tells us outright what a character is like.
A writer can also show a character indirectly: through what they say, what they do and what they think. Other characters' reactions to them also reveal who they are.
a character who changes over the story, such as a selfish person who learns to care for others.
a character who stays the same from start to finish, even when events happen around them.
draft.remember: Writers build characters by telling and by showing. Dynamic characters change, static ones do not.

a.q: In a story, Priya always waits until the others have eaten before she takes any food for herself. Which method of characterisation is this?
opts: What the character does
Direct description by the narrator
What the character thinks
How other characters react to her
a.why: The reader learns about Priya from her actions, without being told outright. It is not direct description, because no one states that she is generous or considerate.
a.clue: Is the reader told her nature, or shown it by her behaviour?

b.q: At the start of a novel, Tom is proud and mocks his younger sister. By the end he has apologised and he listens to her. How is Tom best described?
opts: A dynamic character, because he changes over the story
A static character, because he is the main character
A static character, because he speaks in every chapter
A dynamic character, because the narrator describes him
b.why: Tom's attitude and behaviour change from the start to the end, so he is dynamic. Being the main character or appearing often does not make a character static or dynamic. What matters is whether the character changes.
b.clue: Compare Tom at the start with Tom at the end.

b.best: A dynamic character, because he changes over the story

problems.detail: The clue 'shown it by her behaviour' practically names the answer 'What the character does', so students can match words instead of applying the idea.

check.summary: The card, the remember line and both questions are accurate and match the chapter. The only issue is that the clue for question a gives the answer away by mentioning her behaviour.
